analysis:
On 5 June 2021 (World Environment Day) PM Narendra Modi advanced the national ethanol-blending target to 20% by 2025, from the earlier indicative date of 2030.

PIB states ethanol blending increased from less than 1.5% in 2013-14 to 20% in 2025-26, and that India reached the 20% target five years ahead of the original 2030 schedule. Monthly official figures cited in press reporting showed average blending of 17.98% in February 2025, before the 20% level was reached in March 2025.

The 2025 deadline was met, so the promise is recorded as true.
notes: Original 2030 target comes from the National Biofuel Policy 2018; the claim records the advanced 2025 date the PM announced on 5 June 2021. Wording is from the PMO statement as quoted by Mint, so not marked verbatim. The reference to 'five years ahead of schedule' compares against the original 2030 target, not the advanced 2025 date.
